indicators.note: accommodating means holding a guest inside, so one piece is put within the other

parts.note: to grudge someone something is to envy them it
none is nothing, written as the zero-shaped letter O

explanation.surface: A government minister who bears a grudge and makes room for nobody.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoy is a diplomatic minister sent to represent a government abroad.

explanation.surface: Is a tinker just a skilled craftsman under another name?
explanation.definitionFit: To tinker is to mess about idly at a task; a craftsman who throws clay pots on a wheel makes ceramics.

clue.text: Iron possibly obtained from the moors

indicators.note: something obtained from these letters is made out of them, reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Iron ore dug out of the moorland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron' looks like the metal mined on the moors, but it is the household appliance that presses clothes flat; 'possibly' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes iron is one example of a device that flattens creases out of fabric.

explanation.surface: Requested exactly as had been agreed in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something called for has been requested or demanded; something arranged has been put in sequence or tidied.

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart
to allure is to entice or tempt

explanation.surface: Turning up one's nose at studying something enticing.
explanation.definitionFit: Disdain is scorn, a feeling that something is beneath one.

explanation.surface: Someone thriftily preserving fruit by turning it into jam.
explanation.definitionFit: To save something is to keep it from waste; jam is fruit preserved by boiling with sugar.

indicators.note: dreadfully suggests something done very badly, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Miners being told a tale in a dreadful way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tell' here means tell tales to the authorities, and 'dreadfully' is the anagram signal on FOR MINERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Police informers are people who tell on others, passing secrets to the authorities.

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
to degenerate is to decay or rot

explanation.surface: A painter who joins a company and goes to the bad.
explanation.walkthrough: Jean-Baptiste-Camille Corot was a 19th-century French landscape painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Corot was a French landscape painter of the Barbizon era.

explanation.surface: A Tory who is also an athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue is the colour of Britain's Conservative Party; at Oxford and Cambridge a blue is someone who has represented the university at sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Tory politics is associated with the colour blue; an Oxbridge varsity athlete is awarded a 'blue'.

parts.note: the main is the sea, so this is a window in a ship's side that looks out over the waves

explanation.surface: A grand opening ceremony that everyone overlooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' is an old word for the open sea, not 'principal'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's round side window gives a view of the open sea.

clue.text: Most recent tale to be spun by a good man

indicators.note: a spun tale is twisted round, so its letters are reshuffled

parts.note: ST, short for saint, is the crossword good man

explanation.surface: A good man spinning his newest yarn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be spun' is the anagram signal; 'good man' is the usual crossword shorthand for a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: The newest thing is the one that came along last of all.

parts.note: read as a curved passage a walker goes under, and also the curved part of a person's sole

explanation.surface: A footpath that passes through somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue offers a passageway walkers use, but the curve under the sole of the foot has the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved structure forming a gateway is one; so is the raised curve in the sole of a foot.

explanation.surface: Forever, nevertheless, as a Latin motto might say.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'nevertheless' as 'never the less' and flip both halves to their opposites: 'never' becomes 'ever' and 'less' becomes 'more'.
explanation.definitionFit: In perpetuum is Latin for forever; the opposite of 'never the less' is always greater.

clue.text: Perfectly plain fish is set before the workers

indicators.note: set before says the fish piece is placed ahead of the workers piece

parts.note: the pike is a predatory freshwater fish
a firm's staff are its workers

explanation.surface: A fish is laid out in front of the workforce, plain as can be.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition rests on the idiom 'as plain as a pikestaff', meaning obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'plain as a pikestaff' means utterly obvious, so the word stands for something completely clear.

parts.note: Di is the short form of Diana, with the possessive S
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Princess Diana has left to put on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To disport oneself is to amuse or divert oneself with play.

clue.text: A number in underwear are on the roof!

indicators.note: in puts the number inside the underwear

parts.note: panties are women's knickers
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone's underwear has been flung up onto the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Curved clay roofing tiles that overlap are a common covering for buildings.

parts.note: read as someone who takes livestock, that is a thief of cattle, not someone counting a shop's goods

explanation.surface: The person who does the inventory.
explanation.walkthrough: A stocktaker counts goods in a shop; here 'stock' is livestock and the 'taker' a thief.
explanation.definitionFit: A cattle thief makes off with livestock, the farmer's stock.

clue.text: A French male carrying dope made to strip

indicators.note: carrying means holding something inside, so the dope goes within

parts.note: un is French for a
he is the male pronoun
a clot is a fool or dope

explanation.surface: A Frenchman with drugs on him is forced to undress for a search.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' means the French article and the male pronoun hold the dope between them; 'made to' simply links wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To unclothe someone is to remove their garments.

clue.text: This could well be a trashy little refuse receptacle

indicators.note: could well be suggests these letters might be remade into something else

explanation.surface: A tatty little bin for rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could well be' signals the anagram of A TRASHY.
explanation.definitionFit: A small dish for cigarette ash and stubs is a little container for waste.

clue.text: A woman tucked into smaller portions. Result, slimming success!

indicators.note: tucked into means placed inside, so the woman goes within

parts.note: less means smaller amounts
Anne is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman eats smaller helpings and is rewarded with weight loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked into' looks like eating, but it means ANN goes inside LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinness, a body with little fat, is what dieting aims at.

clue.text: Bearing with beastly home for the garden

parts.note: E, east, is a compass bearing
a den is the lair of a wild animal

explanation.surface: Heading out with an animal's lair as home for the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical paradise where Adam and Eve lived is called 'the garden'.

indicators.note: Sound tells us the word for place is said aloud, giving a word that is pronounced the same

parts.note: a site is a place or location

explanation.surface: A good spot to bring something up.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite is to quote or refer to something.

indicators.note: in places the everything word inside the tow word

parts.note: the clue's word tow, a vehicle being pulled along, read as it stands
all means everything

explanation.surface: Grease everything that is being towed.
explanation.walkthrough: The page reads 'low', an OCR slip for 'tow'. Animal fat used for candles and soap is grease.
explanation.definitionFit: Rendered animal fat used for candles and soap is a kind of grease.

parts.note: a set is a collection of things

explanation.surface: A fee levied on a group of items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' is an attack, as in a cavalry charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge in battle is a sudden assault, the start of an attack.

clue.text: If rest is disturbed there's animosity

indicators.note: a disturbed group of letters is upset and put in another order

explanation.surface: Disturbed sleep leads to bad feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Strife is bitter conflict or discord.

clue.text: Wind blowing lake in South London area

indicators.note: in places the lake inside the London district

parts.note: Tooting is a district of south London
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A gale blowing across a lake in a part of south London.
explanation.walkthrough: TOOTING is a district of south London. 'Wind' is a wind instrument, not weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing a horn or flute idly in short notes is light blowing on a wind instrument.

clue.text: To hold out is just not on with royalty

parts.note: off means unacceptable, not on
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: Refusing to give in is simply unacceptable to the monarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: To offer is to hold something out for another to take.

indicators.note: badly signals that these letters are rearranged poorly

explanation.surface: A shoe that turns out to be badly made.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fashioned has been shaped or crafted.
